steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: Oh... Another sunny day. I don't seem to remember any winters ever being so warm.

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: How wonderful... As long as the wheat we're planting survives the winter and we don't hit a Catastrophe, we'll be self-sufficient next year!

steps.name: Worried Old Woman
steps.text: It's a little too early to celebrate, after all I've been through...

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: Come on, have a little optimism, Babushka! There was a time we thought we'd have nowhere to go, that we'd just die in the barrens! But now, we have our own farm, a house, and hot porridge—

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: Huh? Who's over there...?

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: It's Miss Talulah! And Nine!

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: Miss Talulah, are you helping us pull the weeds?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Talulah, she's talking to you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Oh—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Yes, that's right. Am I doing it wrong?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I saw everyone doing it this way, and the weeds here have grown pretty tall. So tall you can't see the wheat.

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: No, no, you're doing it right. Pulling the weeds out will help make sure the wheat gets enough nutrients to survive the winter—

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: You're such a quick learner!

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Pff.

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: You've already pulled so many, and you haven't hurt a single wheat bud! Looks like you don't need my help anymore.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You taught us well. How's Iakov, by the way?

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: The new medicine he's been taking is very effective, thanks to you! He used to writhe in pain until he fell out of bed at night, but no more.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Be sure to take care of yourself, too.

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: I know. Honestly, this is already much better than what I was expecting, getting to keep him by my side.

steps.name: Happy Peasant Woman
steps.text: Thank you, both of you, and bless the Reunion Movement!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...No need to thank me.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: It's been two years, and you still feel uneasy when people show you their gratitude.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I thought you'd have gotten used to it long ago.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Well, I'm not the one they should be thanking.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Sure enough. They are united under Reunion's banner, but they should actually be thanking themselves.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Not everyone has the courage and ability to rebuild their lives from the rubble.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I hope they'll realize that.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: And you might want to realize how obvious it is when your mind is drifting away.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I was just wondering... when is Hui-chieh going to come back again?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Don't tell me you're worried about her.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Every time she's here, she brings back news.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Catastrophe Messengers avoid this disputed area, and normal ones won't so much as pass through. The information network we've spent two years building up is still far from comprehensive.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm waiting... waiting for Hui-chieh to bring something more real.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: What kind of news do you want to hear?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Anything... I want to know what's actually happening in Ursus right now.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: You don't believe what we saw in the west.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: What, you do?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The upper class gave a little handout out of kindness, and that was enough to quell the anger for the most part, and enough to make those beset by injustice forget to think and resist.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: At the very least, we certainly did not receive any requests for help from the mining districts, whether from the west or even farther away.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Perhaps they just don't know of our existence, or they can't reach us.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Besides, we still have yet to build a truly stable stronghold here.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: But the people here haven't lost hope in us because of it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But they should, Nine.
Talulah looks back in the direction where the sun is hanging high in the sky.
She stares into its light, until her eyes start to hurt.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Even if our village is almost self-sufficient right now, an unforeseen Catastrophe could easily wipe everything out in one fell swoop.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The first couple months saw that happen again and again, and it took much trial-and-error for us to make it here.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But these peaceful days won't last long. I once believed that after our long journey, we'd have more companions leave us than remain. I never would've thought our group would grow larger.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And it's not because we ran into more oppressed people. It's because those who chose us haven't lost faith in us, even if they ought to have.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: All we've done is show them a bit of kindness, and most of them chose to give unconditional trust in return.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Even after they've felt the pain of survival time and again, their barren lands can still yield these emotions more precious than gold?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I can't... After all that, I can't even imagine.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Which is why I started to think... What if it's just how everything is supposed to unfold? This is the truth that these humblest people believe.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: They fall down, then get back up. They fail, and they start over.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: What's your point?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We will fail again, Nine, but I think we don't have to fear this anymore.

spans.text: fail again, Nine, but I think we don't have to fear this anymore.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Well, you're wrong. I've never been afraid of it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But those who walked with us have felt that fear. After all, not everyone has such a grand outlook as you. Many of them just hope to see the next sunrise.

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: Nine, the new suppressant pipeline's finished. Should we put it to use right away?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Valiya.

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: Yeah?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: If I were to tell you we're abandoning this place and heading to Deity Grypherburg, what would you do?

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: Hah! Of course I'm coming with you. Why?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: What about the others?

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: Them too. We knew all along that Reunion wasn't going to stop here.

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: But I don't think all of us should go. Everyone's been doing different things here for a while. Those of us who can fight should go with you, but the rest can still stay here.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Infected Fighter
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Nine, it's just as he said... I think perhaps we're ready now—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We're ready to face the hideous truth hiding behind all that's bright and colorful. After they've long taken root and proliferated, they can't all be pulled at once...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: In such a case, we can only keep pulling away. A second time, and a third time... for as long as we live, until someone finally succeeds.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Now that we know who we must bring together, the time may have come to break these shackles, and we should do it without hesitation.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Uniting all those who can unite, and breaking all chains that should never have chained us...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We need only a single opportunity.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Talulah. Nine.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: It's urgent.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: What is it, Red? It's not like you to look so nervous.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I ran into a group of refugees near the village. They said they're miners who escaped the Far North, and they're here cause they've heard tell of Reunion.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I checked them over. They're unarmed, and they're all Infected. I had them wait at the sentry post. We need you to decide what to do.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: From the Far North? We haven't heard much from there. What do you mean, they 'escaped?'

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Yeah, not much intel ever leaks out of there.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: As for what happened... maybe it's better you hear it from them.

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: Thanks... Thanks for taking us in, kind lady, mister... Are you the Reunion Movement we heard about?

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: I never would've thought... what Rankin told us was true... My goodness...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Slow down. We are Reunion, and we will do what we can to help all our suffering comrades.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Could you please tell us what you've been through?

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: We...

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: There was a massacre in the Far North...
